descriptionModule.briefSummary: This phase I trial studies the best dose and side effects of recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) carrying the human (h) sodium iodide symporter (NIS) and Interferon (IFN) beta (β) genes (VSV-hIFNβ-NIS) in combination with cemiplimab in patients with T-cell lymphoma. A virus, called VSV-hIFNβ-NIS, which has been changed in a certain way, may be able to kill cancer cells without damaging normal cells. Participants will receive a total of three induction therapy cycles, 42 days for each cycle, with isatuximab, bortezomib, lenalidomide and dexamethasone.

Following induction, participants will receive high dose conditioning therapy with melphalan and autologous stem cell transplantation (auto-SCT).

Following auto-SCT, participants will receive maintenance therapy with isatuximab and lenalidomide during 28-day cycles for up to 36 cycles or until unacceptable toxicity, disease progression per IMWG criteria, or withdrawal of consent, whichever occurs first.
armGroups.label: Arm A: Standard of Care Therapy (SOCT)

Participants will receive a total of three induction therapy cycles, 42 days for each cycle, with isatuximab, bortezomib, lenalidomide and dexamethasone.

Following induction, participants will receive lymphodepleting chemotherapy with cyclophosphamide and fludarabine for 3 days, followed by a single infusion of anitocabtagene autoleucel.

Following anitocabtagene autoleucel, participants will receive maintenance therapy with isatuximab and lenalidomide during 28-day cycles for up to 36 cycles or until unacceptable toxicity, disease progression per IMWG criteria, or withdrawal of consent, whichever occurs first.
